NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular business
  hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a recording is
  available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35 (Cox) and
  Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails received
  before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If
  you would like to address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public
  comment, please complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 26, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR HUFF called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by students from the South Coast Interfaith Council’s Jewish Muslim Christian Youth
(JMCY) Program.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

None.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-G AS FOLLOWS BY
  THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF SEPTEMBER 2023

  APPROVED WARRANTS 66612 THROUGH 66649 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $87,586.80; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 090123 THROUGH 090323
  IN THE AMOUNT OF $114,501.33; FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF
  $202,088.13 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF AUGUST 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF AUGUST 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 8, 2023

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 26, 2023
   REVIEWED AND APPROVED.
F.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 12, 2023

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

G.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 4, 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

None.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF
  SEPTEMBER 18, 2023: FOUNDERS PARK ALTERNATIVE

  Recommendation: That the City Council consider the recommendation from the Park
  and Activities Commission, and provide direction to staff.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECTED STAFF TO COMPLETE THE FOUNDER’S PARK PROJECT IN
  PHASES, WITH PHASE 1 TO INCLUDE LANDSCAPING AND
  CONSTRUCTION IN FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 AND PHASE 2 TO INCLUDE THE
  PURCHASE AND INSTALLATION OF THE PLAY EQUIPMENT TO BE
  BUDGETED AND COMPLETED IN FISCAL YEAR 2024-25; AND DIRECTED
  STAFF TO FURTHER REVISE THE SCOPE IF ADDITIONAL COST SAVINGS
  ARE FEASIBLE AND TO AVOID INEFFICIENCIES IN THE COMPLETION OF
  BOTH PHASES THAT COULD CAUSE ADDITIONAL OR REPEAT WORK.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

B.  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE MANAGEMENT SERVICES AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council enter into the attached Agreement with
  Soundskilz, Inc., to provide parade management services for the Peninsula Holiday
  Parade of Lights on December 2, 2023 approved as to the satisfaction of the City
  Attorney.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

MAYOR HUFF appreciated the brainstorming staff has done to try to bring down the costs, and
recommended considering staff or volunteer for judges.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA echoed the Mayor’s comments about trying to keep the cost
down.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved to approve the contract as proposed, to the
satisfaction of the City Attorney, up to $33,000.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 26, 2023
 MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ expressed concern about Pageantry Parades not responding to
the City’s outreach, especially since we’ve worked with them for many years. Staff explained
that they too are concerned and heard from other cities who previous used the company that
they too did not receive any response.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  DIRECTED STAFF TO ENTER INTO THE ATTACHED AGREEMENT WITH
  SOUNDSKILZ, INC., TO PROVIDE PARADE MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR
  THE PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE OF LIGHTS ON DECEMBER 2, 2023
  APPROVED AS TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA reported that she, along with MAYOR HUFF, COUNCIL
MEMBER ZERUNYAN, COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER and several staff members
attended the Cal Cities Annual Conference in Sacramento last week. She also will be attending
the South Bay Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG) Board meeting this Thursday.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ extended New Year wishes to those observing Jewish faith, and
thanked Congregation Ner Temid for extending invitations to the Council for their annual Rosh
Hashanah morning service.

MAYOR HUFF reported that the annual City Celebration held last Saturday was a successful
and well-attended event, including Congressman Ted Lieu, Los Angeles County Supervisor
Janice Hahn, representatives from Senator Ben Allen and Assemblymember Al Muratsuchi’s
offices, Mayor Pat Wilson and Councilmember Bea Dieringer from Rolling Hills, Mayor Pro
Tem John Cruikshank from Rancho Palos Verdes, PVPUSA Board member Sara Deen, PV
Library District representatives and many members of our City Staff. Additionally, the City
defeated the Lomita Sheriff’s Station in the annual Volleyball Match.

MAYOR HUFF also reported that on Wednesday, September 27 at 10am, the City will be
dedicating the Pagliano Perimeter Pathway at Ernie Howlett Park.

MAYOR HUFF reported that the Tracy Austin Doubles Tournament will be held October 13-
15, the Prepared Peninsula Expo will take place on Sunday, October 22 from 10:00 am – 1:00
pm, and the annual Holiday Parade of Lights will be held Saturday, December 2.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Government Code Section 54957
  Title: City Manager (Annual Evaluation)

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 26, 2023
 14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:30 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting in memory of Los Angeles
County Sheriff Deputy Ryan Clinkunbroomer. The meeting was adjourned to Tuesday,
October 10, 2023, at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Regular Meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Britt Huff
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 26, 2023
